changes: Add that the explanatory variable may be used to predict changes in the response variable, as the VCE Unit 2 course frames it.
match.reason: The bank card teaches the same roles (explanatory on the x-axis, response on the y-axis) at the right Year 11 depth, but it says 'explain or influence' rather than the VCE 'predict' wording, so a small wording change is needed.

confirm.reason: The closest bank point, Scatterplots, teaches explanatory and response variables only as part of the broader skill of building a scatterplot (one of its questions is about plotting a coordinate pair), so a focused point on identifying the two variables is better made new.

draft.title: Response and explanatory variables
card: When two numerical variables may be linked, we ask which one might explain or predict the other.
the variable that may explain or predict changes in the other. It goes on the horizontal axis.
the variable that may change in response. It goes on the vertical axis.

Example: a teacher studies hours of study and test score. Hours of study may explain the score, so hours is explanatory and score is the response. Choosing the explanatory variable is a judgement about which could predict the other, and it does not prove that one causes the other.
draft.remember: Explanatory may explain or predict. Response is what changes. Explanatory goes across.

a.q: Mia records the hours of sunshine each day and the number of ice creams sold at her stall in Geelong. She wants to predict sales from sunshine. Which is the response variable?
opts: The price of an ice cream
a.why: Mia wants to predict sales from sunshine, so sales is the response variable. Hours of sunshine is the explanatory variable, the one used to explain or predict.

b.q: Sam collects data on the height of 20 students and the length of their forearms. He wants to predict height from forearm length. Which statement about his scatterplot is correct?
opts: Forearm length goes on the horizontal axis
Height goes on the horizontal axis
Forearm length is the response variable
Either variable can go on the horizontal axis
b.why: Sam predicts height from forearm length, so forearm length is explanatory and goes on the horizontal axis. Height is the response and goes on the vertical axis. The axis is chosen by which variable is used to predict, not by which is bigger.
b.clue: Which variable is being used to make the prediction?

b.best: Forearm length goes on the horizontal axis
